fields.title: Geisha & Floral Micro-Lots Guide
fields.content: Panama Geisha and Ethiopian Geisha varieties cultivated above 1,900 MASL produce intoxicating floral aromatics of jasmine, bergamot, peach, and guava. Best brewed using pour-over V60 or Chemex at 92-94°C with soft water (50-70 ppm) to accentuate volatile floral oils.
fields.tags: geisha, ethiopia, panama, jasmine, pour over, v60, light roast, brew

fields.title: Cold Extraction & Dutch Tower Method
fields.content: Kyoto Dutch cold drip extraction uses ice-cold water dripping drop-by-drop over 12-18 hours. This slow oxidation prevents tannin bitterness while concentrating heavy cocoa esters, whiskey oak notes, and a velvety syrupy mouthfeel.
fields.tags: cold drip, kyoto, cold brew, dutch drip, dark roast, ice, dutch, brew

fields.title: Artisanal Pastry Pairing Science
fields.content: Butter croissants pair impeccably with high-acidity washed Geishas. Rich chocolate pastries like tiramisu and cocoa truffles balance deep volcanic dark roasts like Sumatra Blue Batak and Roasted Hazelnut Truffle Mocha.
fields.tags: pairing, bakery, croissant, tiramisu, chocolate, breakfast, food

fields.title: Ethiopian Traditional Jebena Buna Ceremony
fields.content: Traditional Ethiopian Buna is prepared using clay jebena pots. Green beans are freshly washed, roasted over open charcoal coals, ground fine by hand, and brewed three times (Abol, Tona, Baraka) accompanied by burning frankincense and popped corn.
fields.tags: jebena, buna, ceremony, abol, ethiopian tradition, roasting, clay pot
